O.outcome_detail: fNIRS neural pattern similarity within the mirror neuron system and its subregions

cells.quote: Main effects of emotion valence were observed in the MNS and all its subregions ( F(1, 79) > 12.78, p < 0.002, ƞ2p ≥ 0.139), with greater AUC values for NPS within positive than negative emotions (Fig. 2a), revealing that the MNS and its subregions have more similar neural representation during the imitative learning of positive emotion.
cells.note: The study states that participants were unfamiliar with imitative learning of facial expressions; age is inferred from the adult participant sample and the study does not report an age range.

result.effect: r(79) = 0.278, pFDR = 0.025 for overall MNS; r(79) = 0.337, pFDR = 0.009 for IFG

cells.quote: The results indicated a signiﬁcant positive correlation between behavioral performance changes and NPS changes when imitative learning of positive emotion in the overall MNS ( r(79) = 0.278, pFDR = 0.025, Supplementary Fig. 3) and IFG ( r(79) = 0.337, pFDR = 0.009, Supplementary Fig. 4), but not in the STS ( r(79) = 0.181,p = 0.108) or IPL (r(79) = 0.131, p = 0.245) or during imitative learning of negative emotions ( ps>0 . 2 2 8 ).
cells.note: The study reports measured associations between changes in neural pattern similarity and behavioral performance, not a randomized instructional contrast. Participants were described as unfamiliar with imitative learning of facial expressions; age was not stated.

O.outcome_detail: fMRI representational prediction of emotional versus neutral faces

result.effect: IFG positive-versus-neutral face prediction AUC increase=0.134, permutation p=0.047

cells.quote: Moreover, 10,000 times permutation tests showed that the accuracy of using the IFG as a restriction region for predicting positive and neutral expression faces was signiﬁcantly higher in the post-FISL than inthe pre-FISL session (increase in AUC: 0.134, permutation test p = 0.047).
cells.note: This is the reported long-term transfer effect to emotional-face perception after the month-long FISL course.
